links.outcome: Output consistency across repeated temperature settings for ASR and LLM postprocessing
links.effect: Most models (4 Claude variants, GPT-4.1) were insensitive to temperature (all |Cohen dz| ≤0.15); GPT-4o showed modest dependence (dz=0.139 BERTScore at 0.6 vs 0.0).
links.quote: In contrast, the 4 Claude variants and GPT-4.1 were largely insensitive to temperature, with all Holm-adjusted P values exceeding .05 except a single isolated comparison for Claude 3.7 Sonnet at temperature 0.8 CER (Holm-adjusted P <.001); however, the corresponding effect size for that comparison (Cohen d z =0.064) indicates a practically negligible difference

links.outcome: ASR transcription error (CER/WER) for code-switched nursing notes, including drug-name utterances
links.effect: Baseline ASR CER 0.2336, WER 0.3709; drug-name subset baseline CER 0.3230; after dictionary+Claude Sonnet 4 postprocessing CER 0.0820 overall, 0.0837 in drug subset.
links.quote: However, surface-form accuracy metrics revealed considerable room for improvement, with a WER of 0.3709 and a CER of 0.2336.

links.outcome: ASR errors at Korean-English code-switching points in speech
links.effect: Code-switching points accounted for a disproportionate share of transcription errors; English terms rendered as Korean phonetic forms; baseline CER 0.2336.
links.quote: Analysis of error patterns revealed that code-switching points, where speakers transitioned between Korean and English within single utterances, accounted for a disproportionate share of transcription errors.
